Good afternoon. Thank you, Madam Chair. So here's a name city internal auditor. This report is requesting approval of the terms of reference for the investigation of service disruptions in Saskatoon Transit.

In the winter of 2021-22, Saskatoon Transit faced bus shortages causing service disruptions, which resulted in not meeting the planned level of service. On April 25, 2022, the city council approved the city internal auditor's office to conduct an independent investigation with a close-world arrangement.
The objectives of this investigation is to conduct a root cause analysis of service disruptions which happen in the winter of 2021-22.
And provide cost effective and practical recommendations to avoid future disruptions in Saskatoon Transit.
In preparation of the terms of reference, I met with the Transit Administration. Other stakeholders, including the Amalgamated Transit Union 615 and bus riders of Saskatoon.
The objective of the meetings was to obtain input on areas which should be the focus of the investigation.
The scope of this investigation will be limited to the assessment of service disruptions pertaining to the fixed route buses.
And therefore access transit will be excluded from the investigation.
The areas to be covered within the scope of the investigation will include preventative maintenance, repairs, sourcing of parts, internal and external communication and reporting.
Age of bus fleet compared with other municipalities, availability and allocation of resources, impact of fusion, staff overtime, process documentation and workplace culture.
I would like to highlight a few key assessment criteria specifically related to preventative maintenance and repairs and sourcing of parts.

For preventative maintenance and repairs, the investigation will assess compliance with the preventative maintenance requirements, use of private sector for repairs, effectiveness of the decision to keep the buses on the road with check engine light on.
In fact of the decision to move staff from service line to apprentice and setting, tracking and monitoring of performance measures and targets for maintenance and repairs.
For sourcing of parts, the investigation will assess the timeliness in the ordering and receipt of parts.

The effectiveness of the part sourcing process, effectiveness of the vendor follower process to ensure timely delivery of parts, availability of required parts in the market, availability and competency of store staff, management oversight and inventory management.
As part of the investigation, meetings will be conducted with the transit administration and other stakeholders and detailed review of documents and records will be done.
The investigation team will meet with transit administration to discuss primary findings throughout the investigation to ensure there is lead time for fixing immediate issues before the next winter.
A detailed investigation report will be presented to the Standing Policy Committee on Transportation in the October 3rd, 2022 public meeting.
The detailed terms of reference has been attached in the appendix of the report.
